V-CARD-EVAL.title: Evaluator Verification Against Treys Library
V-CARD-EVAL.question: Does the pure-NumPy vectorized evaluator exactly match Treys on category and relative hand ordering?
V-CARD-EVAL.method: Evaluated 5000 random 7-card hands against Treys library evaluator
V-CARD-EVAL.caveats: Comparison maps category 9 (Royal Flush) to class 1 alongside Straight Flushes per Treys specification.

V-CARD-COUNTS.title: Exact 5-Card and 7-Card Hand Combinatorics
V-CARD-COUNTS.question: Do exact combinatorial category frequencies sum to total combinations C(52,5) and C(52,7)?
V-CARD-COUNTS.method: Exact combinatorial counting verified against standard textbook enumeration
V-CARD-COUNTS.caveats: Hands are unordered; royal flushes separated as category 9 from other straight flushes (category 8).

V-BENCH-PROBS.title: Three Fundamental Benchmark Probabilities
V-BENCH-PROBS.question: Do theoretical benchmarks match reference poker probabilities?
V-BENCH-PROBS.caveats: Pocket pair set calculation assumes unseen cards are drawn without replacement from remaining 50 cards.

I-CARD-SPEED.title: Vectorized Evaluator Performance Benchmark
I-CARD-SPEED.question: What is the throughput of the pure-NumPy 7-card hand evaluator?
I-CARD-SPEED.caveats: Measured on host CPU in quick mode.

V-IDENTITY-1N.title: Exchangeability Identity Check E[Equity] = 1/n
V-IDENTITY-1N.question: Does the combo-weighted average equity share per player exactly equal 1/n across all table sizes n=2..9?
V-IDENTITY-1N.method: Full-table simulated deals (5,000 deals per n) verifying chip and payout conservation
V-IDENTITY-1N.caveats: Holds exactly due to exchangeability of uniformly dealt cards across seats.

V-EQUITY-BENCH.title: Starting Hand Equity Benchmarks and Rank Inversion
V-EQUITY-BENCH.question: Do AA, 72o, and 32o equities match informal literature benchmarks, and does 32o surpass 72o at multiway tables?
V-EQUITY-BENCH.method: Vectorized Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations per hand/table size)
V-EQUITY-BENCH.caveats: Source of initial figures is informal simulation video; our own computation is the formal reproducible evidence.

V-EXACT-MC.title: Exact River Enumeration vs Monte Carlo Agreement
V-EXACT-MC.question: Does Monte Carlo estimation agree with exhaustive combinatorial enumeration on partial boards?
V-EXACT-MC.method: Exhaustive enumeration of all 45,540 deals on turn board compared to Monte Carlo sampling
V-EXACT-MC.caveats: Tested on heads-up turn board with flush and straight draws.

V-STATS-TOOLKIT.title: From-Scratch Statistics Toolkit Numerical Verification
V-STATS-TOOLKIT.question: Do the from-scratch NumPy implementations of special functions, distributions, and parameter fits match SciPy/Statsmodels within numerical tolerances?
V-STATS-TOOLKIT.method: Direct comparison on grid of test points and simulated datasets against SciPy/Statsmodels
V-STATS-TOOLKIT.caveats: All algorithms implemented in pure NumPy and standard library without external numerical packages.

V-UCI-EVAL.title: Evaluator Verification on Full UCI Poker Hand Dataset
V-UCI-EVAL.question: Does our pure-NumPy 5-card evaluator achieve 100% agreement against all 1,025,010 labelled UCI hands?
V-UCI-EVAL.method: Mapped UCI suit (1-4) and rank (1-13) encoding to internal base-15 representation and evaluated every hand across both training (25,010) and testing (1,000,000) splits.
V-UCI-EVAL.caveats: UCI cards are ordered (480 royal flush instances per suit); suit mapping is Hearts=1, Spades=2, Diamonds=3, Clubs=4; Ace is rank 1.

F-UCI-GOF.title: Goodness-of-Fit Table 1: UCI Hand Class Frequencies vs Exact Multinomial Distribution
F-UCI-GOF.question: Do the UCI training and testing splits follow the natural combinatorial distribution of 5-card poker hands?
F-UCI-GOF.method: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test comparing observed frequencies to exact combinatorial probabilities with sparse bin pooling (min expected count >= 5.0) and Monte Carlo multinomial cross-check.
F-UCI-GOF.caveats: Training split was deliberately designed by UCI authors with over-sampled rare hands (5 Straight Flushes, 5 Royal Flushes), leading to chi-square rejection (p=0.024). Testing split follows natural multinomial probabilities with high precision (p=0.990).

F-PHH-TABLESIZES.title: Real-Play Table Size and Showdown Participant Distribution (PHH HandHQ)
F-PHH-TABLESIZES.question: What is the distribution of table sizes and showdown participants in real multi-player online cash games?
F-PHH-TABLESIZES.method: Extracted seats dealt and players revealing showdown cards from 2009 HandHQ games across 600NL and 1000NL stakes.
F-PHH-TABLESIZES.caveats: Convenience sample of July 2009 mid-high stakes games (Absolute Poker, PokerStars); 6-max and Heads-up predominate.

F-PHH-WINNING-CAT.title: Real-Play Showdown Winning Hand Category Distribution and Selection Bias
F-PHH-WINNING-CAT.question: How does the distribution of winning hands in real showdowns differ from theoretical random card dealing?
F-PHH-WINNING-CAT.method: Calculated winning hand category frequencies from HandHQ showdowns and compared against random deal combinatorics.
F-PHH-WINNING-CAT.caveats: Selection bias is severe: players fold weak holdings across three betting streets, heavily suppressing High Card showdowns.

F-PHH-TIGHTNESS-Q.title: Effective Player Tightness Estimated from Real-Play Showdowns
F-PHH-TIGHTNESS-Q.question: What effective preflop tightness q best reproduces the observed winning hand distribution at showdown?
F-PHH-TIGHTNESS-Q.method: Grid search over top q fraction of starting hands (q in [0.10, 1.00]) under heads-up equity ranking, minimizing Total Variation distance.
F-PHH-TIGHTNESS-Q.caveats: Fitted q reflects cumulative selection across all betting rounds, not solely initial preflop VPIP.

F-G1-IID-GAP.title: Table Size Dynamics and Failure of Independent Order-Statistic Model (G1)
F-G1-IID-GAP.question: Does the tie-aware independent maximum model F(x)^n accurately predict winning hand categories and split pot frequencies in Texas Hold'em?
F-G1-IID-GAP.method: Simulated 5,000 full deals per table size n=2..9, recorded winning hand category and split pot occurrences, and compared against discrete_order_stat_max using exact single-player 7-card probabilities.
F-G1-IID-GAP.caveats: Shared community board cards create positive correlation among hands. The independent model systematically overestimates expected winning rank and grossly overestimates split pots at the category level because full 5-card kickers break ties.

F-G2-EQUITY-TABLE.title: Equity Distribution across Table Sizes and Beta Goodness-of-Fit (G2, Table 2)
F-G2-EQUITY-TABLE.question: Does the 1/n conservation identity hold across all table sizes, and does a Beta distribution fit the equity distribution of random starting hands?
F-G2-EQUITY-TABLE.method: Computed full 169-class equity table for n=2..9, verified combo-weighted mean equals 1/n, and fitted Beta distributions with bootstrap CIs, KS tests, and Table 2 chi-square GOF.
F-G2-EQUITY-TABLE.caveats: Combo-weighted mean equals exactly 1/n by exchangeability. The fraction of profitable hands shrinks from ~40% at heads-up to ~28% at 9 players as pot equity becomes heavily concentrated in premium hands.

F-G2-RETURN-STAKED.title: Return per Unit Staked Dynamics and Premium Hand Scaling
F-G2-RETURN-STAKED.question: How does the expected return per unit staked R_n = n*E_n - 1 evolve as table size grows from heads-up to full ring?
F-G2-RETURN-STAKED.method: Calculated R_n = n * E_n - 1 for all 169 hands across table sizes n=2..9 within the equal-contribution baseline model.
F-G2-RETURN-STAKED.caveats: Equal contribution baseline assumes all players contribute 1 chip to pot; real betting dynamics involve folds and raises.

F-G7-RANK-STABILITY.title: Starting Hand Rank Stability and Multiway Reordering (G7)
F-G7-RANK-STABILITY.question: Do starting hand rankings remain stable as table size n expands, and which hand archetypes change rank?
F-G7-RANK-STABILITY.method: Calculated Spearman rho and Kendall tau rank correlations of all 169 classes across n=2..9, tracked rank changes, and mapped to a 13x13 grid.
F-G7-RANK-STABILITY.caveats: Rank correlation decays from 1.000 to 0.829 (Spearman) and 0.647 (Kendall). Suited connectors and small pairs rise up to 67 positions due to straight/flush multiway potential, while weak unsuited broadways drop.

F-G7-FORMULA-FIT.title: Candidate Equity Formula Selection, Fitting, and Validation (G7)
F-G7-FORMULA-FIT.question: Can starting hand equity across table sizes n be accurately estimated by a simple by-hand power law within 1.0 percentage point tolerance?
F-G7-FORMULA-FIT.method: Fitted models M0..M4 with Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation on fit seed, tested a smooth law beta_n = 1 + b*sqrt(n-2), and validated out-of-sample on seed 1337.

phone_recipe: Step 1: Look up or estimate heads-up equity p2. Double it: x = 2 * p2.
Step 2: Raise x to the power beta_n = 1.0 + 0.23 * sqrt(n - 2).
Step 3: Divide by table size n (e.g. for n=6, divide by 6).

F-G7-FORMULA-FIT.caveats: M1 achieves mean MAE of ~1.7 pp across multiway games and reproduces the collapse of premium pairs (AA falls from 85% to 49% at 6-max). M4 further reduces MAE to ~1.1 pp by incorporating suitedness and gap penalties.

F-G5-LUCK-SAMPLESIZE.title: G5: Poker Profit Distribution, CLT Convergence, Power Analysis, and Brownian Ruin
F-G5-LUCK-SAMPLESIZE.question: How does per-hand poker profit deviate from normality, what sample size is needed for CLT convergence and strategy separation, and how accurate is the continuous Brownian ruin approximation?
F-G5-LUCK-SAMPLESIZE.method: Simulated limp-or-fold showdown game with rotating blinds, computed moments of N-hand sums, analytical vs Monte Carlo power calculation, and Brownian ruin vs simulated random walks.
F-G5-LUCK-SAMPLESIZE.caveats: Limp-or-fold game model abstracts post-flop betting and raises; actual poker variance is higher due to deep-stack multi-street betting.

F-G6-WAITING-TIMES.title: G6: Waiting Times for Rare Hands, Goodness-of-Fit Table 3, and PGF Moment Derivations
F-G6-WAITING-TIMES.question: Do waiting times for rare starting hands follow geometric distributions, how well do PGF derivatives recover moments, and is Poisson adequate for rare hand frequency?
F-G6-WAITING-TIMES.method: Simulated 2-card deals, binned chi-square Goodness-of-Fit Table 3 with pooled tail bins, numerical PGF central differences at s=1, and Poisson vs Negative Binomial fits per 1,000 hands.
F-G6-WAITING-TIMES.caveats: Simulation deals cards with replacement between hands; within a single deal cards are dealt without replacement.

F-G3-STREET-MARTINGALE.title: G3: Equity Across Streets as a Martingale, Variance Decomposition, and Rao-Blackwell
F-G3-STREET-MARTINGALE.question: Does equity across streets satisfy the martingale property, how does variance decompose by street, and how large is the Rao-Blackwell variance reduction?
F-G3-STREET-MARTINGALE.method: Simulated street-by-street multi-player rollouts, evaluated exact turn river enumerations, computed variance increments, and compared raw MC vs flop-conditioned estimators.
F-G3-STREET-MARTINGALE.caveats: Simulation uses flat distributions for opponent holdings; opponent actions (bets/folds) create information that alters conditional distributions.

F-G4-OPPONENTS-RANGES.title: G4: Opponent Tightness Ranges and Starting Hand Equity Shifts
F-G4-OPPONENTS-RANGES.question: How does opponent preflop range width q in {8%, 20%, 33%, 50%, 100%} affect starting hand equity and formula calibration across table sizes?
F-G4-OPPONENTS-RANGES.method: Monte Carlo equity estimation against range-filtered opponent holdings under heads-up and multiway rankings across n=2, 6, 9.
F-G4-OPPONENTS-RANGES.caveats: Simulation assumes opponent preflop range equals showdown range; in actual play post-flop betting produces further selection bias.

F-G8-BLIND-COST.title: G8: Blind Costs and Table Size Break-Even Ranges
F-G8-BLIND-COST.question: How does mandatory blind cost (1.5/n bb) influence strategy profitability from heads-up to full ring, and why do tight ranges bleed heads-up?
F-G8-BLIND-COST.method: Analyzed closed-form blind drain model 1.5/n bb/hand, verified against simulated limp-or-fold sessions across n=2, 6, 9.
F-G8-BLIND-COST.caveats: Assumes fixed blinds without ante or structure escalation; folding players forfeit posted blinds.

F-G8-TABLE-SELECTION.title: G8: Table Selection ANOVA Interaction and Strategy Rankings Across Mixes
F-G8-TABLE-SELECTION.question: Does focal strategy performance depend on opponent lineup through a statistically significant Strategy x Opponent Mix interaction?
F-G8-TABLE-SELECTION.method: Two-way balanced ANOVA with permutation-calibrated interaction F-test on a 5 focal strategies x 4 opponent mixes factorial design.
F-G8-TABLE-SELECTION.caveats: Opponents play fixed preflop ranges; actual players adapt their play style dynamically to focal opponents.

V-PORTABLE-NB.title: Portable Notebook Execution and Fresh-Environment Verification
V-PORTABLE-NB.question: Can a reader receiving only the submission files (notebook, requirements, CSVs, data files) execute the entire notebook from first cell to last with zero errors, both with and without the holdem_lab package?
V-PORTABLE-NB.method: Executed holdem_lab.ipynb via jupyter nbconvert across both normal mode (USE_PACKAGE=True) and an isolated fresh environment (/tmp/holdem_submission_test) with holdem_lab completely unavailable (USE_PACKAGE=False).
V-PORTABLE-NB.caveats: Submission environment requires Python 3.11+ and dependencies specified in submission/requirements.txt.

F-G9-DEMO-LOGS.title: G9: Interactive Demo Calibration & Wisdom-of-Crowds (Convenience Sample)
F-G9-DEMO-LOGS.question: Does simulation aid improve player equity calibration and how well does the crowd average track true equity?
F-G9-DEMO-LOGS.method: Evaluated 18 decisions across 6 seats from interactive demo logs.
F-G9-DEMO-LOGS.caveats: Educational convenience sample from interactive demo; play chips only; outside core formal findings.
